stem: Out of the dates given below, which date constitutes a Pythagorean triplet?
solution: A Pythagorean triplet satisfies \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\). For 15, 8, 17: \(8^2 + 15^2 = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17^2\). Hence 15/8/17 forms a Pythagorean triplet.

stem: \(\sin\theta \times \operatorname{cosec}\theta = \) ?
solution: Since \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\), we get \(\sin\theta \times \operatorname{cosec}\theta = \sin\theta \times \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta} = 1\).

stem: Slope of the X-axis is ____.
solution: The X-axis makes an angle of \(0^\circ\) with the positive direction of the X-axis, so its slope \(= \tan 0^\circ = 0\).

stem: A circle has radius 3 cm. Then the length of its largest chord is ____.
solution: The largest chord of a circle is its diameter \(= 2r = 2 \times 3 = 6\) cm.

subtopic: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
stem: If \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR\) and \(AB : PQ = 2 : 3\), then find the value of \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle PQR)}\).
solution: By the theorem of areas of similar triangles, \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle PQR)} = \dfrac{AB^2}{PQ^2} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\).

stem: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm touch each other externally. Find the distance between their centres.
solution: When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centres equals the sum of their radii \(= 5 + 3 = 8\) cm.

stem: Find the side of a square whose diagonal is \(10\sqrt{2}\) cm.
solution: For a square, diagonal \(= \sqrt{2}\times\text{side}\). \(\therefore \text{side} = \dfrac{\text{diagonal}}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\) cm.

stem: Angle made by a line with the positive direction of the X-axis is \(45^\circ\). Find the slope of that line.
solution: Slope \(= \tan\theta = \tan 45^\circ = 1\).

stem: In the figure, \(\angle ABC\) is inscribed in arc ABC. If \(\angle ABC = 60^\circ\), complete the following activity to find \(m\angle AOC\).
solution: \(\angle ABC = \dfrac{1}{2}\, m(\text{arc } AXC)\) (inscribed angle theorem). \(\therefore 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\, m(\text{arc } AXC)\). \(\therefore m(\text{arc } AXC) = 120^\circ\). But \(m\angle AOC = m(\text{arc } AXC)\) (property of the central angle). \(\therefore m\angle AOC = 120^\circ\).
figureNote: p-03: circle with centre O; inscribed angle ABC (B on the major arc) and central angle AOC subtended by chord AC; point X marked on the minor arc AC.

stem: In right-angled \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle C = \theta\). Complete the following activity to find the value of \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta\).
solution: By Pythagoras theorem, \(AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2\). Dividing both sides by \(AC^2\): \(\dfrac{AB^2}{AC^2} + \dfrac{BC^2}{AC^2} = \dfrac{AC^2}{AC^2}\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac{AB}{AC}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{BC}{AC}\right)^2 = 1\). But \(\dfrac{AB}{AC} = \sin\theta\) and \(\dfrac{BC}{AC} = \cos\theta\). \(\therefore \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\).
figureNote: p-04: right-angled triangle ABC, right angle at B, with the angle marked \(\theta\) at vertex C.

stem: In the figure, \(\square ABCD\) is a square and a circle is inscribed in it so that all sides of the square touch the circle. If \(AB = 14\) cm, complete the following activity to find the area of the shaded region.
solution: Area of square \(= (\text{side})^2 = 14^2 = 196\) cm\(^2\). The circle is inscribed in the square, so its radius \(= \dfrac{14}{2} = 7\) cm. Area of circle \(= \pi r^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 154\) cm\(^2\). Area of shaded region \(=\) Area of square \(-\) Area of circle \(= 196 - 154 = 42\) cm\(^2\).
figureNote: p-05: square ABCD with a circle inscribed touching all four sides; the four corner regions between the square and the circle are shaded. AB = 14 cm.

subtopic: Area of Sector and Segment of a Circle
stem: Radius of a sector of a circle is 3.5 cm and the length of its arc is 2.2 cm. Find the area of the sector.
solution: Area of sector \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times r \times (\text{arc length}) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3.5 \times 2.2 = 3.85\) cm\(^2\).

stem: Find the length of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle if its remaining sides are 9 cm and 12 cm.
solution: By Pythagoras theorem, hypotenuse \(= \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15\) cm.

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: In the figure, \(m(\text{arc } NS) = 125^\circ\) and \(m(\text{arc } EF) = 37^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle NMS\).
solution: \(\angle NMS\) is the angle between two secants drawn from the external point M. \(\angle NMS = \dfrac{1}{2}\,[\,m(\text{arc } NS) - m(\text{arc } EF)\,] = \dfrac{1}{2}(125^\circ - 37^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{2}\times 88^\circ = 44^\circ\).
figureNote: p-06: external point M with two secant rays; the upper secant cuts the circle at E (near) and N (far), the lower secant cuts it at F (near) and S (far). Intercepted arcs NS and EF.

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm. \(\left(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\right)\)
solution: Surface area of a sphere \(= 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7^2 = 4 \times 22 \times 7 = 616\) cm\(^2\).

stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), ray BD bisects \(\angle ABC\) with \(A - D - C\), and seg \(DE \parallel\) side BC with \(A - E - B\). Complete the following activity to show that \(\dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{AE}{EB}\).
solution: In \(\triangle ABC\), ray BD bisects \(\angle B\). \(\therefore \dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{AD}{DC}\) ...(I) (property of the bisector of an angle of a triangle). In \(\triangle ABC\), \(DE \parallel BC\). \(\therefore \dfrac{AE}{EB} = \dfrac{AD}{DC}\) ...(II) (basic proportionality theorem). From (I) and (II), \(\dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{AE}{EB}\).
figureNote: p-07: triangle ABC with ray BD bisecting angle B (D on AC) and segment DE parallel to BC (E on AB); the two equal angles at B are marked.

stem: Chords AB and CD of a circle with centre P intersect at point E. Draw seg AC and seg BD, then complete the following activity to prove that \(AE \times EB = CE \times ED\).
solution: In \(\triangle CAE\) and \(\triangle BDE\): \(\angle AEC \cong \angle DEB\) (vertically opposite angles); \(\angle CAE \cong \angle BDE\) (angles inscribed in the same arc CB). \(\therefore \triangle CAE \sim \triangle BDE\) (AA test of similarity). \(\therefore \dfrac{AE}{DE} = \dfrac{CE}{BE}\) (corresponding sides of similar triangles). \(\therefore AE \times EB = CE \times ED\).
figureNote: p-08: circle with centre P; chords AB and CD intersecting at interior point E; seg AC and seg BD drawn (dashed) forming triangles CAE and BDE.

stem: Determine whether the points \(A(1, -3)\), \(B(2, -5)\), \(C(-4, 7)\) are collinear.
solution: Slope of AB \(= \dfrac{-5-(-3)}{2-1} = \dfrac{-2}{1} = -2\). Slope of BC \(= \dfrac{7-(-5)}{-4-2} = \dfrac{12}{-6} = -2\). Since slope of AB \(=\) slope of BC and point B is common to both lines, the points A, B, C are collinear.

stem: \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle LMN\). In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB = 5.5\) cm, \(BC = 6\) cm, \(CA = 4.5\) cm. Construct \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle LMN\) such that \(\dfrac{BC}{MN} = \dfrac{5}{4}\).
solution: Since \(\dfrac{BC}{MN} = \dfrac{5}{4}\), each side of \(\triangle LMN\) is \(\dfrac{4}{5}\) of the corresponding side of \(\triangle ABC\): \(MN = \dfrac{4}{5}\times 6 = 4.8\) cm, \(LM = \dfrac{4}{5}\times 5.5 = 4.4\) cm, \(LN = \dfrac{4}{5}\times 4.5 = 3.6\) cm. Construction: (1) Construct \(\triangle ABC\) with \(BC = 6\) cm, \(AB = 5.5\) cm, \(CA = 4.5\) cm. (2) Draw ray BX making an acute angle with BC, on the side opposite to A. (3) Mark 5 equal points \(B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4, B_5\) on ray BX. (4) Join \(B_5C\). (5) Through \(B_4\) draw a line parallel to \(B_5C\) meeting BC at N; then \(BN = \dfrac{4}{5}BC = 4.8\) cm, so N corresponds to the vertex M-side and BN = MN. (6) Through N draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA at L. \(\triangle LMN\) (with the vertex at B, side MN = 4.8 cm) is the required triangle similar to \(\triangle ABC\) in the ratio \(4 : 5\).

stem: Seg PM is a median of \(\triangle PQR\), \(PM = 9\) and \(PQ^2 + PR^2 = 290\). Then find QR.
solution: By Apollonius' theorem, \(PQ^2 + PR^2 = 2PM^2 + 2QM^2\), where \(QM = \dfrac{1}{2}QR\). \(\therefore 290 = 2(9)^2 + 2QM^2 = 162 + 2QM^2\). \(\therefore 2QM^2 = 128 \Rightarrow QM^2 = 64 \Rightarrow QM = 8\). \(\therefore QR = 2 \times QM = 16\).

stem: Prove that: 'If a line parallel to a side of a triangle intersects the remaining sides in two distinct points, then the line divides the remaining sides in the same proportion.'
solution: Given: In \(\triangle ABC\), line \(l \parallel\) side BC intersects side AB at P and side AC at Q. To prove: \(\dfrac{AP}{PB} = \dfrac{AQ}{QC}\). Construction: Draw seg PC and seg BQ. Proof: \(\triangle APQ\) and \(\triangle PQB\) have equal heights (from Q and B onto line AB share the same distance region). \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle APQ)}{A(\triangle PQB)} = \dfrac{AP}{PB}\) ...(I) (triangles with equal heights, areas proportional to bases). Similarly \(\dfrac{A(\triangle APQ)}{A(\triangle PQC)} = \dfrac{AQ}{QC}\) ...(II). Now \(\triangle PQB\) and \(\triangle PQC\) have the common base PQ and lie between the same parallel lines PQ and BC, so they have equal areas: \(A(\triangle PQB) = A(\triangle PQC)\) ...(III). From (I), (II) and (III), \(\dfrac{AP}{PB} = \dfrac{AQ}{QC}\).

stem: If \(\dfrac{1}{\sin^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\cos^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\tan^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\cot^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\sec^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta} = -3\), then find the value of \(\theta\).
solution: Rewrite each reciprocal: the expression becomes \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \sec^2\theta - \cot^2\theta - \tan^2\theta - \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta\). Group as \((\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta) - (\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta) - (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)\). Using \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1\) and \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\): \(1 - (\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta) - 1 = -3\), so \(\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta = 3\). Since \(\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta\): \(1 + 2\tan^2\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \tan^2\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \tan\theta = 1\). \(\therefore \theta = 45^\circ\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: A cylinder of radius 12 cm contains water up to a height of 20 cm. A spherical iron ball is dropped into the cylinder and the water level rises by 6.75 cm. What is the radius of the iron ball?
solution: Volume of water displaced (rise) equals the volume of the sphere. \(\pi r_{\text{cyl}}^2 h = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). \(\therefore 12^2 \times 6.75 = \dfrac{4}{3} r^3\). \(144 \times 6.75 = 972 = \dfrac{4}{3} r^3\). \(\therefore r^3 = \dfrac{972 \times 3}{4} = 729\). \(\therefore r = 9\) cm. The radius of the iron ball is 9 cm.

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle with centre O and radius 3 cm. Draw tangent segments PA and PB through a point P outside the circle such that \(\angle APB = 70^\circ\).
solution: Since PA and PB are tangents, \(OA \perp PA\) and \(OB \perp PB\), so \(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\). In quadrilateral OAPB, \(\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 90^\circ - 90^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\). Construction steps: (1) Draw a circle with centre O and radius 3 cm. (2) Draw two radii OA and OB such that \(\angle AOB = 110^\circ\). (3) At A draw a ray perpendicular to OA, and at B draw a ray perpendicular to OB. (4) The two perpendicular rays meet at point P. Then PA and PB are the required tangent segments, and \(\angle APB = 70^\circ\).

stem: \(\square ABCD\) is a trapezium with \(AB \parallel CD\). The diagonals of the trapezium intersect at point P. (a) Draw the figure using the given information. (b) Write any one pair of alternate angles and one pair of opposite (vertically opposite) angles. (c) Write the names of the similar triangles with the test of similarity.
solution: (a) Trapezium ABCD with \(AB \parallel CD\); the diagonals AC and BD intersect at point P. (b) Alternate angles (\(AB \parallel CD\) with transversal AC): \(\angle BAP \cong \angle DCP\). Opposite (vertically opposite) angles at P: \(\angle APB \cong \angle CPD\). (c) In \(\triangle APB\) and \(\triangle CPD\): \(\angle BAP \cong \angle DCP\) (alternate angles) and \(\angle APB \cong \angle CPD\) (vertically opposite angles). \(\therefore \triangle APB \sim \triangle CPD\) (AA test of similarity).

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O. AOC is a diameter of the circle and AT is a tangent at A. (a) Draw the figure using the given information. (b) Find the measures of \(\angle CAT\) and \(\angle ABC\) with reasons. (c) Are \(\angle CAT\) and \(\angle ABC\) congruent? Justify your answer.
solution: (a) Circle with centre O; AOC a diameter; AB a chord; AT the tangent at A. (b) \(\angle CAT = 90^\circ\), because the tangent at a point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius (here the diameter AC) drawn to the point of contact. \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\), because it is an angle inscribed in a semicircle (AC being a diameter, the angle in the semicircle is a right angle). (c) Yes. Since \(\angle CAT = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\), we have \(\angle CAT \cong \angle ABC\).
